title: streak-based stream bundler with progressive KV reclamation
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: introduce a low-latency, GPU-friendly batch formation heuristic for streaming chat that groups short-turn 'streaks' of tokens into transient micro-bundles while progressively reclaiming cold KV cache to avoid OOMs and reduce tail latency. This ticket covers design, implementation, observability, and a staged rollout behind a feature flag. The heuristic targets scenarios where many concurrent short turns (1-20 tokens) create fragmentation and KV pressure on the slab allocator, and where strict per-request latency SLOs (e.g., p99 < 200ms) must be preserved.
acceptance_criteria: Streak bundler enabled behind runtime feature flag with default off
P99 end-to-end latency for streaming short-turn workload does not regress more than 5% compared to baseline at current load profiles
GPU memory pressure (ephemeral allocation high-water) reduced by >= 12% on the synthetic 'short-turn burst' workload
KV cache reclamation triggers only when bundle size > threshold and is bounded to per-request microbudget (<= 1ms additional scheduling overhead)
Rollout plan completed: canary (5% host capacity) -> grad increase -> org-wide with telemetry showing stable error/latency and no OOMs
Automated unit and integration tests for bundler, KV-reclaim contract, and slab allocator interaction present in CI
decisions: Use 'streak' as the primary grouping primitive: consecutive short turns from a session within a configured window (default 120ms) are candidates for bundling
Bundle max size default: 12 short turns or 256 tokens, whichever first
Progressive KV reclamation will evict least-recently-used KV slots in micro-slices (configurable slice size) to avoid long pause times
Do not evict pinned KV (pinning happens for active rollouts or evaluation sessions)
Integrate with existing slab allocator's watermark hooks to apply reclamation before GPU OOM is imminent, not reactive after failure
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (Design): finalize parameters (streak window, bundle thresholds, kv-slice size) and simulate on historical traffic traces (Perf/trace-team) - 3d
Phase 2 (Runtime): implement bundler in request-queue layer with priority-preserving insertion and microbudget accounting - 5d
Phase 3 (KV): extend KV manager with progressive_reclaim(slice_tokens) API and integrate with slab allocator watermarks - 4d
Phase 4 (Tests): add synthetic harness for short-turn bursts, fuzz KV reclaim under spike, unit tests for microbudget enforcement - 3d
Phase 5 (Canary): enable feature flag on small fleet, capture metrics and logs, iterate - 5d
Phase 6 (Rollout): staged increase and monitor for 72 hours at each step - ongoing
rollout_plan: Feature flagged; default OFF in production
Canary: 5% of servers for 72h; collect latency, error, kv-evict-count, gpu-memory-high, OOM events
Stepwise: 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with 72h observation windows and rollback criteria
Rollback triggers: p99 latency +10% sustained over 30m, error rate spike > 0.5%, first OOM reproducibly attributable to reclaiming logic
Post-rollout: enable telemetry dashboard and add alerting for kv-slice-throttle and reclaim-failure
metrics: p50/p95/p99 end-to-end latency (streaming completions, short-turns subset)
Bundle hit rate (fraction of short-turns that joined a streak bundle)
Average scheduling overhead introduced by bundler (ms)
OOM incidents attributed to KV pressure
risks: Aggressive bundling could increase tail latency for requests that cannot be coalesced quickly
Reclamation could evict KV needed by near-future tokens causing re-computation overhead
Interaction with other schedulers (priority decay, preemption) may produce starvation for low-priority flows
Incorrect slice sizing could either cause frequent small evictions (inefficient) or long pauses (latency regressions)
test_plan: Unit tests for streak detection logic (edge cases: time jitter, out-of-order arrival)
Integration: synthetic short-turn burst workload derived from production traces (30m replay) comparing baseline vs bundler
Chaos: force slab watermark crossing during bundling to validate progressive reclaim tolerates pressure without OOM
Performance bench: measure microbudget overhead and confirm per-request scheduling cost <= 1ms on p99
End-to-end canary validation with production traffic subset and A/B comparison for 7 metrics above
